messages:
Alex Monroe: looping in the team — Zetta wants to run a short migration POC from RivalAPI. They're concerned about prompt parity and response diffs. Can we get an initial plan?
Priya Patel: thanks Alex. main asks from Zetta so far: 1) API compat layer to minimize app changes 2) cost mapping (tokens -> pricing) 3) security questionnaire answers + SOC2 evidence 4) latency SLOs for their EU customers
Sam K. (Zetta): confirming — we also need model fallbacks (cheap vs high-qual) and a way to reproduce current prompts exactly. timeline: 2-week POC preferred.
Samir Gupta: ok on compat layer — we can expose a RivalAPI-compatible endpoint that accepts their params and maps to rw-compat model. Need to know which Rival model they use and any custom headers.
Sam K. (Zetta): using rival/goliath-13b, custom header X-Customer-Context, and a small embedding call for rerank.
Jo Chen: for prompt parity we should capture both request/response diffs and tokenization differences. propose: run 200 representative prompts through both systems, diff outputs, and surface top-3 divergence patterns.
Miguel Rivera: +1. I'll set up the eval harness. can we get a seed dataset from Zetta? ideally 200-400 prompts with expected outputs or acceptance criteria.
Sam K. (Zetta): sending dataset now via secure file share. also have a security questionnaire attached.
sec-bot: Security questionnaire received (Zetta). Ticket: SEC-2026-045. Assigned: Priya Patel.
Priya Patel: I'll own the questionnaire. quick notes: they asked about KMS/HSM, data retention, access logs, and VLAN isolation. We have standard answers but will need SOC2 report attach and a short note on Private deployment options.
Alex Monroe: finance question: Zetta asked how Rival token pricing maps to Redwood. what's the easiest way to translate their TUs to our tokens?
Samir Gupta: rough approach: map Rival input+output TU to token counts using same tokenizer. We'll run a tokenization script on their sample prompts and measure average tokens per request. Then estimate cost with our per-token SKU.
Priya Patel: also note: Dedicated offers committed capacity which might beat their current pricing if volume is predictable. I'll prepare a compare sheet.
Miguel Rivera: deploy-bot created a POC workspace for zetta-poc-1782.
deploy-bot: workspace zetta-poc-1782 created in eu-west-1, assigned to Miguel Rivera and Samir Gupta.
Jo Chen: integration detail: Rival's streaming chunk format differs. We'll provide a shim that emits identical chunk boundaries if they set `compat: true` header. Need to validate client reconnection behavior.
Sam K. (Zetta): streaming parity is important — clients rely on delimiting tokens.
Samir Gupta: I'll prototype the shim. sample mapping (very rough):
```
# Rival -> Redwood
Rival: { "stream": true, "model": "goliath-13b" }
Redwood: { "stream": true, "model": "rw-compat-13b", "headers": { "X-Compat-Mode": "rival" } }
```
Jo Chen: we'll also include a flag to preserve Rival stop-token behavior.
Priya Patel: enterprise blocker: they need IP allowlist + SAML SSO + audit logs. Private deployment can cover IP + data residency. SAML is supported via our enterprise console. I'll confirm logging retention options.
Sam K. (Zetta): great. SOC2 report and SAML guide would unblock legal.
sec-bot: SOC2 Type II report link shared with participants via secure link.
Alex Monroe: next steps: 1) Samir/Miguel: prototype shim + eval harness (deliverable: diff report + sample API mappings) by EOD +3. 2) Priya: pricing compare + security answers by EOD +4. 3) Jo: streaming parity checklist + stop-token verification. 4) Miguel: provision Dedicated trial if needed.
Samir Gupta: ack, starting shim. I'll post a small reproduction snippet once ready.
Miguel Rivera: I'll provision a Dedicated trial window but will hold until Zetta confirms volume.
Priya Patel: sharing draft pricing: if they hit >50M tokens/month, Dedicated reserved capacity becomes cost-effective vs pay-as-you-go. Sending numbers to the channel privately. :money_with_wings:
Sam K. (Zetta): thanks all. we'll review diffs and security notes and circle back. happy to extend POC if more time needed.
Alex Monroe: thanks team — I'll follow up with Zetta on timeline and make sure legal gets SOC2 link. :thumbsup:
Samir Gupta: posting first shim snippet in thread in ~2 hours.
Jo Chen: adding an item to confirm rate-limit headers mapping (`X-RateLimit-Remaining` parity).
Sam K. (Zetta): one last Q: how do you handle randomness/temperature parity? We rely on deterministic seeds for some tests.
Samir Gupta: currently our runtime supports `seed` for deterministic sampling on compatible samplers. We'll document exact behavior per model variant.
Priya Patel: closing notes: I'll attach the completed security questionnaire and the SAML integration guide once done.
Alex Monroe: perfect — keep updates here.
